summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and extensive vascular disease was admitted for evaluation of whole-body tremors and worsening pain in her right index finger with dry gangrene. The tremors, which had resolved by admission, were attributed to metabolic deregulation related to her kidney disease, with neurology finding no evidence of a neurological event. A CT head showed chronic small vessel disease but no acute process. Her finger showed distal necrosis without signs of active infection, and she declined an arteriogram. Plastic surgery determined no urgent intervention was needed, and she was managed conservatively with pain control. She underwent dialysis during admission, remained stable, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up for possible digital amputation and vascular evaluation.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Acquired absence of left leg below knee
